caveats: grocery means FRESH/perishable food retail. Mapping v1.0.0 wrongly included 'Retail Sales of General Merchandise and Non-Perishable Food' (dollar/variety/corner stores with no perishables), inflating grocery by 1,355 geocoded rows: 6,616 -> 5,261, a 20.5% overstatement of fresh-food access on the South and West Sides. Corrected in v1.1.0.
These are LICENSES, not businesses. See licenses_are_not_businesses.

medical_health (274) is NOT a measure of health care access. Chicago does not license clinicians (Illinois IDFPR does); the dataset contains no physician, dentist, clinic, optometry or chiropractic tokens at all. Structural omission with a reason, not a zero.
financial_services drops 43.3% of rows for missing coordinates because debt collection and tax prep licensees are often registered at out-of-city head offices. Not a complete storefront count.

other (38.9%) is deliberate: automotive and fuel (no bucket exists in this taxonomy), peddlers and street performers (no fixed site), mobile food (address is the commissary, not where the truck operates), shared kitchens (excluded from grocery per spec), wholesale food, special-event permits, and 3,152 rows whose business_activity is null so no sector can be read.

Brand name does not determine category; the filed activity does. The SUBWAY at 7901 S Yates Blvd is grocery because the city's own record files it under 'Retail Sales of Perishable Foods'. Overriding the record by brand would be fabrication.
The 4,376 rows without coordinates are an explicit omission, never a zero. They were not placed at a centroid, ZIP centre, or any imputed point.

Categorization uses exact string matching, never substring. Substring matching produced real false positives on this data: 'Provide 4 or More Parking Spaces' contains 'spa'; 'Live Theatrical' contains 'therap'; 'Cert. of Fitness' (demolition contractor) contains 'fitness'.
